description: Astronaut Reproductive Health & Fertility Risk Assessment System
summary: Doctor Space is an web app that helps a crew member without medical training monitor health on a long space mission. It addresses the challenge of astronaut health software with three tools. First, a guided ultrasound: printed sticker pads with steel dots and a probe collar with small magnets keep the probe at the right spot and angle, so a non-doctor can scan the heart and abdomen. The app shows a simulated image, asks plain-language questions, and returns one HEALTH ALERT result: normal, review or urgent, with next steps. Second, an SOS mode with a CPR coach, an AED chest-patch guide and a medical kit that stays locked until it is authorised. Third, vitals tracking against each astronaut's own baseline, including sleep, mood, heart rate, blood pressure, temperature, glucose and hemoglobin, plus Bone Watch and a pre-flight fertility bank register. It matters because NASA lists distance from Earth, cardiovascular and bone changes as key risks, and no doctor may be on board. The app never chooses a drug or a dose.
details: What it does: Doctor Space is a static web app (HTML, CSS and vanilla JavaScript) that works offline in any browser. Crew members use pad-guided ultrasound, a simulated ultrasound viewer, a HEALTH ALERT triage, an SOS emergency mode, wellness vitals, Bone Watch and a fertility bank register. How it works: Seven anatomical sticker pads, each located by measuring from the sternal notch, carry steel dots. Magnets in a probe collar dock to the dots and hold position and angle, not pressure. A MagniScan model shows hold force, field at the skin and a safety factor against the public 400 mT static-field limit. Plain-language answers go through rule-based logic to give normal, review or urgent, with next steps. SOS: CPR coach (about 100 to 120 compressions per minute, 5 to 6 cm deep), AED pads held at the standard chest positions by magnetic frames, and a medical kit that opens only after a ground order and a five-item check. The app never picks a drug or a dose. NASA risks addressed: cardiovascular adaptation (cardiac scan, vitals against a personal baseline), spaceflight bone changes (Bone Watch with a magnetic heel pad), distance from Earth and limited medical support (guided scan, SOS), radiation (pre-flight fertility bank register for sperm, eggs and embryos), sleep and behavior (wellness trends), and anemia (hemoglobin trend). Creative part: magnets replace "find the spot by feel", so a non-doctor can repeat the same scan. Tools: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Python (pad sheet PDF, slide deck), GitHub Pages. SI tools helped write the code, text and graphics. Images and data are simulated. This is a concept prototype, not a validated medical device.
